title: Milestoning Markov-jump dynamics: Stationary properties, thermodynamic consistency, kinetic hysteresis, and fluctuation symmetries
authors: Tassilo Schwarz, David Hartich, Aljaž Godec
abstract: We derive an exact coarse graining of generic Markov-jump processes into observable semi-Markov dynamics. Exact results for waiting-time distributions for jumps between observable states are derived and proved that these decompose into conditionally independent dwell and transition times. Dwell times are proved to be a local property of mesostates - they depend on the initial but not final state. Conversely, transition-path times depend on both states, trigger kinetic hysteresis, and, under suitable conditions on the hidden sub-network, are shown to obey a reflection symmetry. We characterize the stationary properties of the milestoned dynamics, prove its thermodynamic consistency, and demonstrate robustness to milestone positioning. Surprisingly, even in the limit of a time-scale separation rendering the observed dynamics approximately Markovian, the effect of kinetic hysteresis on the dissipation persists. A minimal example shows how the results lay the foundation for inferring affinities of hidden dissipative cycles from observations of transition-path times.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theory for exactly mapping underlying Markov-jump dynamics onto observable semi-Markov processes via 'milestoning.' It rigorously characterizes the resulting kinetics by decomposing waiting times into dwell and transition components. The key findings establish thermodynamic consistency, quantify kinetic hysteresis, and provide methods to infer hidden physical affinities from observed time statistics.
main_problem: The core problem is deriving an exact, thermodynamically consistent coarse-graining of underlying Markov-jump processes into observable semi-Markov dynamics (milestoning). This addresses how memory effects arise when observing a system only at discrete points in time.
main_result: The theory successfully decomposes the waiting time distribution into conditionally independent dwell and transition times, proves its thermodynamic consistency, and demonstrates that kinetic hysteresis persists even when the observed process approaches Markovian behavior.
method: The authors use rigorous mathematical derivations involving generator matrices, Laplace transforms, and renewal theory to analyze the joint probability densities of state transitions across hidden intermediate states.
model_or_system: The model is a generic ergodic Markov-jump process on a full state space $\Omega$, which is partitioned into observable states ($\Omega_{	ext{obs}}$) and unobserved hidden states ($\Omega_{	ext{hidden}}$). The dynamics are analyzed by constructing an effective semi-Markov generator matrix.
key_observables: Waiting-time distributions, dwell times, transition-path times, steady-state entropy production rate ($\dot{\sigma}$), and the affinity ($A_{ij}$) between states.
important_parameters: Time-scale separation limits ($\lambda/\kappa 	o \infty$), barrier heights ($B$), driving intensities ($M$), and the number of parallel hidden mechanisms ($V$).
main_assumptions: The underlying microscopic dynamics satisfy detailed balance (or are analyzed under conditions that allow for thermodynamic consistency checks). The analysis relies on specific structural assumptions about how hidden states connect observed nodes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate model structures, the manifestation of kinetic hysteresis via non-zero KL divergence in waiting time densities, and numerical validation showing the recovery of entropy production rates using milestoning estimators.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the mathematical framework for coarse-graining (Chunk 1), deriving the decomposition of waiting times into dwell/transition components (Chunk 2), proving thermodynamic consistency and reflection symmetry properties (Chunk 3), generalizing to multiple parallel hidden mechanisms (Chunk 4), and finally applying these results to continuous systems like diffusion on a ring potential (Chunk 5).
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, general theoretical tools for analyzing non-equilibrium steady states in complex biological or chemical systems where direct observation is impossible. The rigorous connection between coarse-graining, memory effects, and fundamental thermodynamic quantities like entropy production is highly relevant to open quantum system modeling.
